source_facts: - The `action.yml` inputs MUST keep their names, defaults, and meanings: `repo-token` (default `${{ github.token }}`), `configuration-path` (default `.github/labeler.yml`), `sync-labels` (default `false`), `dot` (default `true`), and the multiline `pr-number`.
cases.atomic_claim: action.yml declares inputs repo-token (default ${{ github.token }}), configuration-path (default .github/labeler.yml), sync-labels (default false), dot (default true), and multiline pr-number with unchanged names, defaults, and meanings.

source_facts: - The `action.yml` outputs MUST keep their names and meanings: `new-labels` and `all-labels`, each a comma-separated list.
cases.atomic_claim: action.yml declares outputs new-labels and all-labels, each described as a comma-separated list, with unchanged names.

coverage.surface: label configuration YAML schema accepted by the action

source_facts: - The label configuration structure MUST stay the same: top-level label names mapped to arrays of match objects using `changed-files`, `head-branch`, and `base-branch`, with optional `any` and `all` groupings, plus the top-level options `changed-files-labels-limit` and `max-files-changed`.
cases.atomic_claim: A config mapping top-level label names to arrays of match objects using changed-files, head-branch, and base-branch, with optional any and all groupings and top-level options changed-files-labels-limit and max-files-changed, is accepted unchanged.

source_facts: - The action MUST use the standard GitHub Actions runtime interface: read inputs from `INPUT_*` environment variables, read the event payload from `GITHUB_EVENT_PATH`, and append outputs to the file named by `GITHUB_OUTPUT`.
cases.atomic_claim: Given INPUT_-prefixed variables, a GITHUB_EVENT_PATH file, and a GITHUB_OUTPUT path, the Go binary reads inputs from INPUT_*, reads the event payload from GITHUB_EVENT_PATH, and appends outputs to GITHUB_OUTPUT.

coverage.surface: GitHub REST and GraphQL calls issued by the action

source_facts: - GitHub API semantics MUST be preserved: REST `issues.addLabels`, paginated REST `pulls.listFiles`, REST `pulls.get`, REST `repos.getContent` with base64 decoding, and the GraphQL `removeLabelsFromLabelable` mutation.
cases.atomic_claim: The action issues POST /repos/{owner}/{repo}/issues/{n}/labels, paginated GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/pulls/{n}/files, GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/pulls/{n}, GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/contents/{path} with base64 decoding, and a GraphQL removeLabelsFromLabelable mutation.

coverage.surface: changed-file glob and branch pattern matching

source_facts: - Changed-file globs MUST keep minimatch semantics, including the `dot` option and `!` negation patterns. Branch patterns MUST be treated as JavaScript regular expressions.
cases.atomic_claim: With dot=false a glob `**/*.ts` does not match `.hidden/x.ts` while a glob `.github/**` matches `.github/workflows/x.yml`; a `!docs/**` pattern negates; a branch pattern `^feature/.*$` is evaluated as a JavaScript regular expression.

source_facts: - Failure behavior MUST be preserved: an unexpected error is logged and fails the action with the error message; a 403 unauthorized error on a label update surfacing the `issues: write` permission hint; and a `Resource not accessible by integration` error downgraded to a warning plus a failed step.
cases.atomic_claim: An unexpected error is logged and fails the step with its message; a 403 unauthorized label update surfaces the issues: write permission hint; a `Resource not accessible by integration` error is downgraded to a warning plus a failed step.

source_facts: - If a changed file matches a label's `changed-files` rules, the action MUST add that label, supporting all four combinations: `any-glob-to-any-file`, `any-glob-to-all-files`, `all-globs-to-any-file`, and `all-globs-to-all-files`.
cases.atomic_claim: For a changed file matching a label's changed-files rules under any-glob-to-any-file, any-glob-to-all-files, all-globs-to-any-file, or all-globs-to-all-files, that label is added.

source_facts: - `any` rules MUST match when at least one option matches; `all` rules MUST match when every option matches; every match object for a label MUST match before the label is applied.
cases.atomic_claim: A label matches only when every match object matches; an any block matches when at least one option matches and an all block matches only when every option matches.

source_facts: - With `sync-labels: true`, the action MUST remove configured labels that no longer match, in a single GraphQL mutation per pull request. With `sync-labels: false`, it MUST NOT remove labels.
cases.atomic_claim: With sync-labels true, configured labels that stop matching are removed in exactly one GraphQL removeLabelsFromLabelable mutation per pull request; with sync-labels false no label is removed.

source_facts: - Labels absent from the configuration MUST never be removed, and labels added concurrently by another actor MUST be preserved.
cases.atomic_claim: Labels not present in the configuration are never removed, and labels concurrently added by another actor remain present in all-labels.

source_facts: - If the label set exceeds 100 labels, the action MUST apply only the first 100 and log a warning listing the excess labels.
cases.atomic_claim: When more than 100 labels apply, only the first 100 are applied and a warning lists the excess labels.

source_facts: - If `max-files-changed` is set and the changed-file count exceeds it, file-based labeling MUST be skipped, branch-based labels MUST remain active, and existing changed-files labels MUST be left untouched.
cases.atomic_claim: With max-files-changed set below the changed-file count, changed-files labels are skipped, branch-based labels still apply, and existing changed-files labels are left untouched.

source_facts: - If `changed-files-labels-limit` is set and the count of new changed-files labels exceeds it, all new changed-files labels MUST be skipped for that run. The limit counts only labels not already on the pull request, and a count equal to the limit is still applied. When both options are set, `max-files-changed` is evaluated first.
cases.atomic_claim: When the count of new changed-files labels exceeds changed-files-labels-limit, all new changed-files labels are skipped; a count equal to the limit still applies; max-files-changed is evaluated first when both options are set.

source_facts: - A label definition containing any changed-files rule MUST be treated as a changed-files label for both `max-files-changed` and `changed-files-labels-limit`.
cases.atomic_claim: A label definition containing at least one changed-files rule is treated as a changed-files label for both max-files-changed and changed-files-labels-limit.

source_facts: - The action MUST read the configuration path locally when the file exists; otherwise it MUST fetch the file through `repos.getContent` and decode the base64 content.
cases.atomic_claim: When the configuration path exists locally the action reads it from disk; otherwise it fetches it through repos.getContent and base64-decodes the content.

source_facts: - Configuration keys other than `changed-files`, `head-branch`, `base-branch`, and the two top-level options MUST be ignored with an informational message. Invalid configuration values, such as a negative or non-integer limit or a malformed `changed-files` block, MUST fail with a descriptive error.
cases.atomic_claim: Unknown configuration keys produce an informational message and are ignored, while a negative or non-integer limit or a malformed changed-files block fails with a descriptive error.

source_facts: - `pr-number` MUST accept newline-separated values: blank entries are ignored, each valid entry is a positive integer after trimming, and invalid entries MUST produce a warning and be skipped. When `pr-number` is empty, the action MUST use the pull request number from the event payload.
cases.atomic_claim: Newline-separated pr-number values are trimmed, blank entries ignored, valid positive integers accepted, invalid entries warned and skipped; when empty, the event payload pull request number is used.

source_facts: - Invalid `pr-number` warnings MUST escape non-printable characters (for example as `\xNN`) in the reported value.
cases.atomic_claim: An invalid pr-number containing a non-printable character is reported with the character escaped as \xNN in the warning.

source_facts: - Pull requests that cannot be fetched, or that have no changed files, MUST produce a warning and be skipped.
cases.atomic_claim: A pull request that cannot be fetched, or that has no changed files, produces a warning and is skipped.

source_facts: - When a label addition fails with a server error, the action MUST verify whether the requested labels were actually applied before failing.
cases.atomic_claim: When adding labels returns a 5xx server error, the action re-reads the issue labels and verifies the requested labels were actually applied before deciding to fail.

source_facts: - A failed bulk removal MUST fail with an error identifying the affected configured labels and the pull request.
cases.atomic_claim: A failed bulk removal fails with an error naming the affected configured labels and the pull request number.

source_facts: - If the configuration file cannot be fetched, the action MUST warn about the missing file and access rights, then log the error and fail the step.
cases.atomic_claim: If the configuration file cannot be fetched, the action warns about the missing file and access rights, logs the error, and fails the step.

source_facts: - `new-labels` MUST list only labels added by the run; `all-labels` MUST list the resulting label set after the run, capped at the 100-label limit. Both MUST be written to `GITHUB_OUTPUT` as comma-separated values, with existing labels first and newly matched labels appended in configuration order.
cases.atomic_claim: new-labels lists only labels added by the run; all-labels lists the resulting label set capped at 100; both are written to GITHUB_OUTPUT comma-separated with existing labels first and newly matched labels appended in configuration order.

source_facts: 1. The migration MUST NOT remove required public capabilities or change their contracts outside the stated goal.
cases.atomic_claim: All prior public capabilities and contracts remain available after migration and none are removed or changed outside the stated goal.

source_facts: 4. Changes MUST be limited to the migrated source scope, the target-language sources, dependency and build configuration, and supporting assets needed to build and run the Go action.
cases.atomic_claim: Changes remain limited to the migrated source scope, the Go target sources, dependency and build configuration, and supporting build assets, with unrelated repository files untouched.

source_facts: 7. You MUST NOT skip checks, remove assertions, weaken comparisons, or hardcode evaluation inputs or outputs to fake compliance.
cases.atomic_claim: Checks and assertions are retained and comparisons are not weakened, and no evaluation input or expected output is hardcoded to fake compliance.
